task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2c) on REQ-170's implementation. REQ-170's own text explicitly names SECURITY-REVIEWER as a hard gate. This requirement's design produced this pipeline's most severe WASM finding to date: decision 0014's timeout-containment claim is live-verified FALSE -- a hung guest permanently leaks a thread from wasmex's shared, node-global native worker pool, with no BEAM-side way to reclaim it, and a live-reproduced scenario showed 32 concurrent hangs starving an unrelated guest call. This finding was already independently reproduced by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at Step 1b (see step-01b-code-design-validator.json) -- your job now is NOT to re-litigate that finding, but to review the SHIPPED CODE's honest handling of it and confirm no security-relevant defect exists in what was actually implemented. Read the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req170-wasm-wallclock-timeout.md) and the real shipped code (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex, lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex) in full before verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm plugin_interface.ex is genuinely untouched (git diff --stat against main) -- the design's entire safety story for AC3 rests on this file's existing, already-shipped algorithm being unmodified.

Confirm plugin_handler.ex's extension is genuinely additive-only: handle_node/1 reads one new node_config key with a safe default (5_000ms, matching wasmex's own prior implicit default -- so a caller who does NOT set timeout_ms gets IDENTICAL behavior to before this change, no silent behavior change for existing callers).

Confirm CallTimeout.classify/1's substring-matching is robust -- re-verify the two literal strings it matches against genuinely, currently match what plugin_interface.ex's handle_yield_result/4 produces (read that function's real current source yourself), and assess whether a guest-controlled value could ever influence the classified string in a way that causes a false classification (this mirrors REQ-169's SECURITY-REVIEWER's own Rust-source-level check for classify_call_result/1 -- apply the same rigor here).
Confirm the moduledoc's divergence disclosure is present in the shipped module (not just the design doc) and does not soften or omit the node-wide-exhaustion finding.

Assess the security implication of this diff's own honest limitation: since guest execution itself is NOT terminated (only the caller's wait is bounded), does this diff's own scope create any NEW security exposure beyond what REQ-165's PluginHandler already had (i.e., is this diff neutral-to-positive from a security posture, or does it introduce something new that needs mitigation before merge, even though the deeper fix -- pool exhaustion -- is correctly out of scope and filed separately)?

Cross-check against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8 explicitly -- INV-3 (untrusted-runtime resource limits/containment) is squarely this diff's subject matter, and this diff's own honest disclosure that a documented containment primitive doesn't work is directly relevant to INV-3's adequacy.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: SECURITY-REVIEWER gate on REQ-170's shipped code: PASS. All 7 acceptance-criteria checks in the handoff independently re-verified against the real diff (git diff main...HEAD), not trusted from the design doc or ELIXIR-DEV's self-report. No blocking defect found.

invariant_assessment.INV-1_tenant_data_isolation: NOT-APPLICABLE. Diff touches no Ecto schema, no migration, no query against a business table -- lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex (new) and plugin_handler.ex (extended) operate purely on ExecutionContext.node_config (an in-memory map) and wasmex NIF calls. No tenant-scoped table/schema/migration reached.
invariant_assessment.INV-2_server_side_field_authorisation: NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type touched; S4 has not started.
invariant_assessment.INV-3_untrusted_runtime_sandboxing: APPLIES (decision 0014 is 'decided' 2026-08-23, S5 is in progress -- the 'deferred until S5's decision record exists' condition is now met, same mechanism as the INV-1 applicability-note precedent). Verified: this diff introduces NO new host-capability-reachable function and widens NO ambient access -- plugin_handler.ex's only change is reading one additional node_config key ('timeout_ms') that controls the CLIENT-SIDE wait bound on an already-existing call; capability_gate.ex and module_registry.ex (REQ-167/168's actual allowlist enforcement) are untouched, confirmed by git diff. Separately assessed (see 'new_exposure_analysis' below) whether making timeout_ms caller-configurable itself widens the resource-exhaustion surface the design's own finding surfaces -- concluded no, it does not, for a stated reason. The diff's own honest disclosure that decision 0014's cited containment primitive does not work is directly relevant to INV-3's overall adequacy conclusion, and is correctly filed (OQ-5, moduledoc, design doc S8) as future scope rather than silently absorbed or fixed out-of-scope in this diff.

invariant_assessment.INV-5_not_found_forbidden_indistinguisha: NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4 has not started.
invariant_assessment.INV-6_new_data_access_paths_prove_scopin: N/A as a distinct data-access-path invariant (no new data-access path introduced) -- satisfied procedurally by this handoff itself, which states applicability per INV-1..INV-8 explicitly as required.
invariant_assessment.INV-7_no_sql_string_interpolation: NOT-APPLICABLE, confirmed by grep. grep -rn 'Repo.query' lib/letflow/engine/wasm/ returns zero hits -- no SQL touched by this diff at all.
invariant_assessment.INV-8_no_unhandled_crashes: APPLIES (diff touches external-I/O-adjacent code -- a NIF call driven by tenant/workflow-authored node_config). SATISFIED. grep -n '^\s*{:ok, .*} = ' on both touched files: zero hits. call_export/3's Wasmex.call_function/4 result is handled by an exhaustive 3-clause case ({:ok,[answer]} / {:ok,other} / {:error,reason}); run_guest/3 uses a `with` chain, no bare pattern match. Manually checked the new caller-controlled timeout_ms path: a malformed/adversarial timeout_ms value (non-integer, negative) reaching GenServer.call inside the dispatched Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 task can only crash that isolated task, which PluginInterface.invoke/2,3's existing, unmodified {:exit, reason} clause (handle_yield_result/4) already converts to a clean {:error, reason} for the caller -- consistent with the let-a-doomed-process-crash-under-supervision carve-out this invariant states, not a shared-process crash.

acceptance_criteria_verification: 1. plugin_interface.ex genuinely untouched -- confirmed independently: `git diff main...HEAD --stat -- lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex` produces empty output. The shipped test suite also asserts this at runtime (plugin_handler_test.exs 'AC6: plugin_interface.ex is unmodified', a live git-diff check against origin/main or main).

2. plugin_handler.ex's extension is genuinely additive-only with a safe, behavior-preserving default -- confirmed by direct read of plugin_handler.ex: handle_node/1 adds exactly one Map.get(node_config, "timeout_ms", @default_wasmex_timeout_ms) read; @default_wasmex_timeout_ms is 5_000, and deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex.ex:419 (`def call_function(pid, name, params, timeout \\ 5000)`) independently confirms wasmex's own real default is exactly 5000ms -- a caller that never sets timeout_ms sees byte-identical behavior to pre-REQ-170 code. read_fixture/1, start_instance/1, handle_node/1's outer error shape, and plugin_interface.ex are all unchanged.

3. CallTimeout.classify/1's substring matching re-verified against plugin_interface.ex's REAL current source (read directly, not from the design doc's quotation): handle_yield_result/4's {:exit, reason} clause (line 217-219) literally produces `"plugin handler " <> inspect(handler) <> " crashed: " <> format_exit_reason(reason)`, and its nil clause (line 221-224) literally produces `"... did not respond within " <> to_string(timeout_ms) <> "ms"` -- both substrings CallTimeout matches against (`"{:timeout, {GenServer, :call,"` and `"did not respond within"`) are exact, current matches, not stale references. format_exit_reason/1 (line 226-232) falls through to plain inspect/1 for the {:timeout, {GenServer, :call, [...]}} shape because its second element is a 3-tuple, not a list, so the is_list(stacktrace) guard clause does not intercept it -- confirmed by reading format_exit_reason/1's own two clauses directly. Guest-controlled-value false-classification risk assessed and found not reachable in the shipped code: the only guest-influenced string reaching classify/1's input is via call_export/3's `{:ok, other} -> {:error, "wasm guest returned an unexpected shape: #{inspect(other)}"}` and `{:error, reason} -> {:error, "wasm guest call failed: #{inspect(reason)}"}` branches, where `other`/`reason` are Wasmtime-produced i32 return values or native trap terms, not arbitrary guest-supplied text (PluginHandler always calls with an empty params list, so no guest-authored string ever flows into the exit-reason machinery classify/1 inspects) -- no realistic guest output can synthesize either literal substring.

4. Moduledoc divergence disclosure re-read directly from the shipped module (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex lines 10-72), not the design doc: present, states the finding at full severity (does NOT soften: 'no BEAM-side mechanism ... can reach or terminate the already-dispatched native execution', 'a saturated pool was live-observed to stall an entirely unrelated, non-hanging guest call'), states explicitly what does NOT hold (decision 0014 point (ii)) and what DOES hold (PluginInterface's outer boundary), and states plainly what the module does NOT claim (execution termination). Test suite enforces this at the doc level (call_timeout_test.exs 'AC6: moduledoc content' describe block, 3 tests via Code.fetch_docs/1).

5. New-exposure analysis: this diff is neutral-to-positive on security posture, no new mitigation required before merge. Reasoning: the design's own live finding (S1.4) establishes that a hung guest's native execution is NEVER reclaimed once dispatched, independent of what timeout_ms value was configured for that call -- the leak is unconditional given any hang, not proportional to timeout_ms. Making timeout_ms caller-configurable therefore does not change how long a leaked native thread stays leaked (permanent either way), and does not change how many concurrent invocations a workflow/tenant can dispatch against the shared pool (PluginTaskSupervisor's concurrency was already unbounded under REQ-165's hardcoded-5s-default PluginHandler, and remains unbounded here -- unchanged by this diff). The attack surface size (an adversarial tenant dispatching many concurrent hangs to exhaust wasmex's node-global TOKIO_RUNTIME) is identical before and after this diff; REQ-165's PluginHandler already had it via the fixed 5000ms default, which is exactly what design S1.5's 32-concurrent-hang reproduction used to demonstrate the exhaustion. The deeper fix (bounding concurrent in-flight invocations) is correctly out of this diff's scope and is filed (design S8/OQ-3, moduledoc) rather than silently absorbed, consistent with this handoff's own instruction not to re-litigate the finding.

6. INV-1..INV-8 cross-checked explicitly above (invariant_assessment). INV-3 is the invariant squarely on point for this diff's subject matter; verified APPLIES (S5 in progress, decision 0014 decided) and SATISFIED -- no new host-capability surface, and the honest disclosure of decision 0014's containment gap is present and undiminished, which is what INV-3's adequacy requires of this diff (the gap itself is a filed finding for a follow-up decision-record amendment, not a defect in THIS diff's shipped code).

7. mix letflow.lint_handoffs run before finishing: 'OK -- 0 new violations across 1268 handoff files (25 pre-existing grandfathered, traced to ISS-0190)'. No new violation attributable to this handoff file.
result.verdict: PASS -- no blocking defect in the shipped code's handling of the wasmex timeout-containment finding. plugin_interface.ex is genuinely untouched, plugin_handler.ex's extension is additive-only with a behavior-preserving default, CallTimeout.classify/1's substrings are verified against the real current plugin_interface.ex source and are not falsifiable by realistic guest-controlled input, the moduledoc's divergence disclosure is present at full severity in the shipped module, and this diff does not widen the resource-exhaustion attack surface beyond what REQ-165's PluginHandler already had. The deeper pool-exhaustion defect (already independently reproduced at Step 1b) is correctly out of this diff's scope and is filed as OQ-5-adjacent evidence rather than fixed here or silently absorbed.
